title: How the eye and brain create vision
intro: Vision requires clear optical surfaces, a working retina, optic nerves and brain processing. Different structures do different jobs; poor sight is not always solved by stronger glasses, and a normal surface appearance cannot exclude disease.

sections.heading: Focusing light
paragraphs: The cornea bends incoming light; the lens adjusts focus. The iris changes pupil size to control entry. Glasses correct certain focusing errors rather than repair every cause of sight loss.

sections.heading: Receiving the image
paragraphs: The retina's rods help in dim light and cones support color and detail. The macula provides fine central vision. Damage to different retinal areas causes different difficulties.

sections.heading: Messages and support
paragraphs: The optic nerve carries signals to the brain. Tears protect the surface, and eye muscles align gaze. Eye pressure relates to fluid production and drainage, not simply blood pressure.

sections.heading: Everyday protection
paragraphs: Use appropriate protective eyewear for hazardous tasks and follow contact-lens hygiene. Have changes assessed; increasing screen brightness does not treat an underlying eye condition.

sections.heading: Urgent changes
paragraphs: Sudden loss of vision or severe eye pain requires emergency assessment. New flashes, many floaters or a shadow across vision need urgent eye care; do not drive yourself with unsafe sight.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira sees a new shadow across her vision. She seeks urgent eye assessment instead of booking only a routine glasses check.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben's reading blur improves with prescribed lenses. He still attends recommended eye checks because focusing and retinal health differ.
